blocking_issues.issue: The bilingual opening presents Poland as the NATO ally with the highest defence expenditure as a share of GDP in the 2026 current context. This is not true under the NATO's July 7, 2026 country-comparable 2026 estimates. Lithuania 5.33%, Estonia 5.10%, Latvia 4.92%, and Poland 4.68%: Poland ranks fourth. The April 2026 IMF box and the March NATO annual report describe 2025 or earlier estimates, not the updated 2026 ranking. The unqualified current superlative is materially false in a central strategic claim.

blocking_issues.issue: The first quantitative bar chart puts GDP growth and HICP inflation (annual changes in percent) on the same axis as the general-government deficit (percent of GDP) but declares a single unit 'annual percentages'/'% anual'. The deficit observations 7.3 and 6.5 are not annual percentage changes; they are deficit magnitudes as shares of GDP. A common 'annual percentage' axis is dimensionally misleading even though the underlying values match the European Commission release.
evidence: EN chart unit: 'annual percentages; fiscal deficit shown as absolute value'; PT-BR chart unit: '% anual; déficit representado em módulo'. Both show GDP 3.6/3.5/2.8, HICP 3.6, deficit 7.3/6.5 on one axis.

European Commission spring forecast 21 May 2026 explicitly separates GDP growth (% year-on-year), HICP inflation (% year-on-year), and general government balance (% of GDP): https://economy-finance.ec.europa.eu/economic-surveillance-eu-member-states/country-pages-including-country-reports/poland/economic-forecast-poland_en
